summary: TSMC is NVIDIA's primary foundry partner for its most advanced GPU wafers (fabless manufacturing); NVIDIA's 10-K explicitly names TSMC as a foundry supplier.
SK Hynix is a named memory (incl. HBM) supplier to NVIDIA per NVIDIA's 10-K; HBM is critical for AI accelerators.
Micron is a named memory supplier to NVIDIA per NVIDIA's 10-K (memory + HBM candidate supplier).

ASML is an INDIRECT supplier: it sells EUV lithography machines to foundries (mainly TSMC) that fabricate NVIDIA chips. ASML does not sell directly to NVIDIA; the link is inferred from the supply chain structure.
Microsoft is widely reported as NVIDIA's largest data-center GPU customer (~19% of NVIDIA revenue per Bloomberg estimates; ~21% of data-center revenue per Epoch AI analysis of Omdia data).

Meta is estimated as NVIDIA's #2 GPU customer (~9-11% of NVIDIA revenue per Omdia/Bloomberg estimates). NVIDIA does not disclose named customers, so this is a high-confidence inference from analyst data.
Amazon (AWS) is estimated as a top-4 NVIDIA customer (~7-8% of NVIDIA revenue per analyst estimates) while also deploying its own custom Trainium/Inferentia chips.
Google (Alphabet) is estimated as a top-4 NVIDIA customer (~7-8% of NVIDIA revenue per analyst estimates); Google also develops TPU accelerators and designs its own chips.

Dell is a major OEM buying NVIDIA GPUs for its AI servers (AI Factory initiative); Dell's AI-server revenue surged to ~$12.9B in Q2 FY2025 on NVIDIA-powered systems. The 10-K also lists Dell's competitor HPE in networking context.
Accenture launched an NVIDIA Business Group (Oct 2024) with 30,000 trained professionals; Accenture's AI Refinery is built on the full NVIDIA AI stack (AI Foundry, AI Enterprise, Omniverse).
ServiceNow expanded its strategic partnership with NVIDIA (Oct 2024) to co-develop agentic AI using NVIDIA NIM Agent Blueprints on the ServiceNow platform.
Snowflake partners with NVIDIA to run NVIDIA NeMo and AI Enterprise software inside the Snowflake Data Cloud for enterprise generative AI (announced 2023 Summit, expanded 2024 GTC).
Cisco and NVIDIA partner on 'Cisco Secure AI Factory with NVIDIA' and co-develop NVIDIA Spectrum-X Ethernet switches (Cisco N9100 series), announced at GTC 2025.
NVIDIA invested $100M in CoreWeave (Apr 2023) and a further $2B (Jan 2026) at $87.20/share; CoreWeave also buys NVIDIA GPUs at scale and builds data centers for NVIDIA.
NVIDIA invested $50M in Recursion Pharmaceuticals (announced July 12, 2023) as part of a multi-year AI drug-discovery collaboration (DGX Cloud, BioNeMo, BioHive supercomputer).

NVIDIA participated in SoundHound's Jan 2017 $75M funding round (per VentureBeat), and a Feb 14 2025 regulatory filing (13F) reported by Reuters shows NVIDIA exited its SoundHound stake in Q4 2024 — the investment relationship is now ended (valid_until set accordingly). Evidence is secondary (Wikipedia + Reuters syndication of the filing), so the relationship is scored inferred.
AMD is NVIDIA's primary direct competitor in data-center GPUs and AI accelerators (AMD MI-series). Explicitly named as a competitor in NVIDIA's 10-K.
Intel competes with NVIDIA in CPUs, AI accelerators (Gaudi) and is entering foundry services. Named as a competitor in NVIDIA's 10-K.
Broadcom competes with NVIDIA in data-center networking (DPUs, Ethernet switches) and custom AI ASICs for hyperscalers. Named in NVIDIA's 10-K.
Qualcomm competes with NVIDIA in edge computing, automotive SoCs and embedded devices. Named in NVIDIA's 10-K as a competitor in those segments.

Oracle and NVIDIA are strategic cloud partners: NVIDIA selected OCI as the first hyperscale cloud for DGX Cloud (2023), the companies co-deliver sovereign AI worldwide (2024), and Oracle is deploying thousands of NVIDIA Blackwell/GB200 GPUs on OCI and DGX Cloud (2025).
